title: Taganrog Fortress
axis: Local X and Z follow the original survey page right and down, turned by the plan compass.
source: Russian State Archive of Ancient Acts 1704 survey, historical bastion site and current OpenStreetMap coastline
identityStatus: The measured historical features are physically gone above grade across much of the cape. The modern memorial marks the approximate third bastion and is independent of the catalogue story point.

features.role: Original dated as-built outline and harbor

terrainContact.basis: Reference from independent terrain source near the central street blocks of the former fortress. Modern terrain approximates general slope and known cape grade.

notes: Engineering sheet RGADA fond 9, inventory 2, file 66, no. 34 shows the named cape, four fronts, three bastions, two half bastions, four ravelins, and the stone moles. The contour, directions and relative sizes follow the survey with its compass and scale. The third-bastion commemoration at Petrovskaya 15 constrains approximate geographic registration.

surveyTrace.scaleBasis: Plan scale reads 0 to 100 Ruten along about 266 normalised pixels. The 1.41 m conversion assumes the 3.766 m Rute used by many German-speakers, consistent with the recorded circumference.
surveyTrace.registrationBasis: Petrovskaya 15 commemoration registers the approximate interior of the third bastion, while modern OpenStreetMap contours and the Qualla Lyall plan provide broad checks only.
